Oldenborn Heritage. The branch that lit up from inside. Festival-spirit, glamour-spirit, the ancestor that taught the people to call something beautiful before they had a word for sacred.

“The world remembered old names. You answered—and you were lit by the answering.”

Lumenwrought. You are the place-soul that learned to wear a mask of light. Folks call you elf, sylph, faerie, depending on what scares them prettier than it scares them honestly. You are the first reason a candle is holy.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Fey).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward PRE (Presence)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.

  • Glamourcast. You can shed dim light in a 1 square radius at will, and snuff it out the same way. Your light is the colour of one specific moment in your past—the GM and you decide which.

description.value:
“You were not beautiful. You were wanted.”

Glamourfield (At Will, Minor). You can create subtle illusions affecting light, sound, scent, or emotional tone. It never overwhelms; it always influences.

Dream Anchor. You have +1 Resolve, and the same edge on checks against metaphysical hazards (slippage, dream traps, Spark backlash).

Primary Attribute: Presence

Every manifestation is an agreement with something. Most casters don't read what they signed. You did, you do, and you keep what you signed for.

Manifestation Discipline: Upkeep / concurrency specialist (5-pt budget — Upkeep ●●●, Misfire ●●, Clarity ●, Reach ●, Signature Mode: Sealed Pact)

Class Identity

Tier cap and footprint stay universal. What you have is holding: more concurrent manifestations sustained at once, lower upkeep on bargained subjects, and the right to renegotiate a misfire instead of eating it. Pactkeepers don't manifest bigger — they manifest more, longer, and in writing.

Class Features

  • Initiation 1 — The Bargain. The Pact slot comes online (+1 Surge per manifestation you sustain at the start of your turn, max +2). While a creature, object, or place is bargained-with as your Pact subject, you may sustain one additional manifestation on or near them at no extra upkeep against your Clarity. Skill rank +1 in two of: Diplomacy, Insight, Intimidation, Lore.

  • Initiation 6 — Renegotiate. When one of your manifestations would misfire, you may instead accept a GM-set narrative debt (a future scene, a future cost, a future favor owed) and treat the manifestation as having succeeded at base tier. The debt is real; the GM's table runs the bill.

  • Initiation 11 — Sealed Pact (Signature Mode). Stance. While the Seal holds, your concurrent-manifestation cap is +2, and you cannot voluntarily drop a manifestation sustained on a pact-bound subject (the seal carries the upkeep, not your moment-to-moment will). Pays ongoing upkeep against your Clarity.

  • Initiation 16 — Ledger Day. 1/Soma Break, transfer one of your sustained manifestations to a willing ally — they pick up upkeep from their Clarity from that point on. The pact moves with the paper, not the person who originally signed.

Doctrines

and the rest of the doctrine ladder. Doctrines remain the depth lane — the Discipline budget above is what you bring to any Pact-shape.

“Reality is consistent because someone keeps the minutes.”

Noise: +3

You are licensed to administer continuity of meaning: what counts as having happened, how strongly the past pulls on the present, and which version of events becomes official.

Esoteric Bias: Divination (Chokhmah) and Illusion (Hod). When casting manifestations from these schools, misalignment penalties are suppressed; aligned casting generates +1 Surge.

Always Prepared Manifestations: Long Ledger, Penalty Clause, Clause Lantern, Standing Oath, Cite Precedent.

Unique Contract: Binding Precedent (see Pactkeeper features).

🧭 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Jurisdiction

Type: Permanent class feature (Level 1)
Purpose: Defines what you are authorized to administer

A Jurisdiction does not grant power directly.
It grants permission.

What Jurisdiction Does

Your Jurisdiction determines:

  • Which situations generate Surge more easily

  • Which effects you may enforce without Noise

  • Which Contracts you can issue by default

  • Which manifestations are considered “in mandate”

Example:

  • A Steward acting on community Loyalty = in mandate

  • A Steward issuing divine sanctions = out of mandate (Pressure risk)

Jurisdiction Is NOT:

  • A resource pool

  • A bonus to rolls

  • A manifestation list restriction

It is a scope limiter and Pressure filter.

“This happened. It matters. Act accordingly.”

When a significant action succeeds or fails, you may establish a Precedent tied to a creature, location, faction, or concept. While active, similar future actions reroll the lowest die if aligned with the precedent, or suffer disadvantage if they violate it. You are not forcing outcomes—you are making contradiction expensive.

Precedent is probability gravity, not mind control.

“Godhood is community service. I’m here to keep the lights on.”

Manifesting (Delegated): You are a full prepared caster. Your manifesting is routed through stabilized civic thoughtforms (tulpas), retired gods, and the Long Quiet—reducing volatility and preventing raw backlash.

Delegated Channeling: When you cast a manifestation, you treat esoteric misalignment as neutral (no penalty). When you cast in alignment with your Jurisdiction, you convert alignment into resources rather than raw power.

Surge

Your Surge bank is capped by tier (4 / 6 / 8 / 10). You bank +1 Surge per manifestation you sustain at the start of your turn (max +2), and spend it from the ◆ Surge menu — Invoke Clause, Binding Writ, Shelter the Bound, Sovereign Writ, and your doctrine's three spends. Everyone's Surge explodes the same way; yours arrives through contracts kept.

Noise

Pactkeepers do not suffer backlash; they accumulate Noise like every manifestant — acting outside your Jurisdiction, overriding consent, forcing outcomes. Noise follows the manifestation rules; several doctrine features add or remove it.

📑 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Precedent

Type: Persistent world state marker
Purpose: Makes outcomes stick and repetition matter

Precedents are not dice. They are flags on reality.

Creating a Precedent

A Precedent is created when:

  • A major action succeeds or fails

  • A Contract is enforced

  • A significant moral or political line is crossed

  • A Pactkeeper explicitly declares one (Archivist specialty)

What a Precedent Does

While active, a Precedent causes:

  • Repeated similar actions to:

    • Suffer disadvantage, or

    • Trigger automatic consequences

  • NPCs and systems to “expect” consistency

  • Reality to resist contradiction

Interacting with Precedent

Pactkeepers may spend Surge to:

  • Cite a Precedent (force rerolls)

  • Lock an outcome as official

  • Suppress contradictory magic or retcons

Archivists gain expanded control over this.

Ending a Precedent

A Precedent ends when:

  • It is superseded

  • It is resolved narratively

  • It is formally revoked

The contract exists to serve the people bound by it.

Mode: Care through obligation / drift: Away

Level 3: Community Contract

No one left behind. Once per scene, when an ally would fall: redirect some of the harm to yourself, stabilize them at once, or grant a protected withdrawal. Spend 1 Surge.

Level 6: Cohesion Pulse

A stabilizing surge through a panicked scene: fear and Loyalty collapse ease, unrest settles, and part of the fallout becomes a small Domain benefit (Soft Power or Loyalty). Spend 1 Surge.

Level 10: Public Works Miracle

Bless a site or community for a day — food stabilizes, shelter holds, calm spreads, structures repair, passage becomes reliable.

Level 10: Mutual Aid Network

Godhood as social work: allies contribute to your Surge through cooperation, and your healing and stabilization spread soft buffers across the group.

Level 14: Integration Charter

Help a community absorb change without breaking: drift fallout eases, minority pressure softens, unity holds under political stress. Noise −1.

Level 18: Civic Apotheosis (Capstone)

For a scene, your community rises into minor civic-deity mode: panic cannot spread, cooperation amplifies, protection and solidarity surge. Spend 2+ Surge.

Oldenborn.

“You are not an elf. You are the memory of a place that learned to walk again.”

Dream-Flesh. You do not sleep. When you rest, you drift into Yesod—symbolic memory-space—unless you choose otherwise. You are immune to magical sleep, and you can always tell when a dream, illusion, or constructed reality is present.

Old Memory, Old Paths. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret ruins, follow ley-lines, identify altered terrain, and sense metaphysical instability. You always know if a place feels remembered, abandoned, or contested (the GM answers vaguely).

Veil-Sight. You perceive the presence of spirits, ghosts, Spark echoes, and noospheric constructs. This grants awareness, not perfect sight.

You Are Remembered. When you first meet a community, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met with reverence, fear, or familiarity. It’s never neutral.

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.

✍ Table rule.

(3rd Level)

Contract: No One Left Behind.

Once per scene, when an ally would fall, you may:

  • Redirect some harm to yourself,

  • Stabilize them immediately,

  • Grant protected withdrawal without pursuit.

This is not dominance.
It is shared burden.

Cost

Spend 1 Surge to amplify (increase stabilization or protection value).

Pushback

Repeated magical rescues may reduce community autonomy over time.

Backline Commander

You don’t need to be closest to steer the fight.

Rules

As a Bonus Action, choose one ally who can see or hear you within 6 squares. That ally may immediately move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.

You can use this technique a number of times equal to your rank bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Soma Break.

🃏 Card — bonus action, rank-bonus uses per Soma Break; target the ally first.

Initiation 6 — Renegotiate. When one of your manifestations would misfire, you may instead accept a GM-set narrative debt (a future scene, a future cost, a future favor owed) and treat the manifestation as having succeeded at base tier. The debt is real; the GM's table runs the bill.

Discipline: passive Concurrency unchanged from Init 1; Renegotiate itself is a narrative reaction resolved at the table when a misfire would land.

description.value:
Breach Specialist

Everything has a seam. Most people just don’t look.

Rules

You gain a rank in Tinkering. If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead.

When you hit an object, door, barrier, or construct with a weapon attack, you may treat the attack as dealing maximum damage to the target’s objects-only resistances (GM adjudication). Once you do, you can’t do so again until the start of your next turn.

⚙ +1 Tinkering. 🃏 Card — the max-damage-vs-objects rider, once per round.

(10th Level)

You bless a site or community for a day.

Choose one infrastructure blessing:

  • Food supply stabilizes.

  • Shelter becomes secure.

  • Calm spreads.

  • Structures repair.

  • Safe passage becomes reliable.

This is not combat power.
This is sustainability.

Cost

Spend 1–2 Surge (scale by scope).

Scope

Blessings operate narratively within reason; they do not invalidate natural law.

Pushback

Communities may begin expecting miracles instead of building systems.
